A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RACQUET study. The complete main texts and appendices A–J support comparison, and retained figures, tables, and equations can be matched despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-response and VLM evaluations, including ambiguity recognition, prompting, saliency, social-bias results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluation of Gemma-3-27B as an automatic response annotator.

M1.justification: The response categories, prompting procedures, adopted Llama-3-70B annotator, and SAM-based referent-matching pipeline remain unchanged. Gemma-3-27B is tested as an alternative evaluator, without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 500 RACQUET-GENERAL pairs, 240 RACQUET-BIAS pairs, and the existing unambiguous-question and real-image checks. The new annotator comparison evaluates the existing response-classification task without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds Gemma-3-27B as an image-aware annotator comparator against the existing text-only evaluator. The models compared in the main ambiguity and bias experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Appendix C.2 evaluation supplies Gemma-3-27B with the original image and question–answer pair, adding an image-aware annotation condition. Existing benchmark settings, human-response collection, and sampling procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic comparison examining the choice of a text-only versus image-aware automatic annotator. The earlier saliency, prompting, sampling, subject-category, and synthetic-versus-real-image analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Agreement reporting through Cohen’s kappa, McNemar testing, and the ten-output sampling count in Appendix E remain unchanged. The new Gemma kappa score adds a result under the existing reporting practice, without introducing uncertainty estimates or changed repeated-run procedures.

E6.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports Gemma-3-27B agreement of 0.67 alongside the retained text-only evaluator agreement of 0.94. Figure 5 adds qualitative human/model responses, and the 87.6% statistic for questions beginning with “What” is omitted. Tables 1–2 and the existing quantitative plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The response definitions and Appendix H’s bounding-box, distance, and maximum-IoU formulation are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions and claims remain the 740-pair benchmark, response-evaluation framework, human–model gap, saliency effects, and stereotypical responses under ambiguity. The abstract is unchanged in substance, and the conclusion retains these claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands discussion of restricted ambiguity coverage, simple-question diversity, and limited prompting strategies. It also adds a rationale for text-only judging, interprets the Gemma result as evidence against VLM evaluators, and discusses fine-tuning and interactive clarification as future directions.

D1.justification: v2 discloses approximately 100 responses reviewed when defining categories, approximately 50 responses per model inspected for accuracy, and manual checking of generated images. It clarifies code/data availability and replaces deferred licensing with an explicit MIT license statement. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bernardi and Pezzelle on VQA language issues, two Zhang papers on interactive clarification, and four references supporting stereotype assignments in Appendix I.2. The central positioning relative to prior ambiguity research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized prose revisions expand methodological explanations, limitations, and future work. Appendix C is divided into prompt and additional-considerations subsections, and affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5 illustrating human and model responses, reformats labels in the bias examples, revises captions, and reflows existing displays. The earlier figures and both tables are retained; quantitative plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through validation sample counts, the additional annotator comparison, expanded limitations, and explicit licensing. The new human/model illustration also clarifies the findings. These are limited gains: the main evidence is unchanged, and the broad conclusion about VLM evaluator reliability exceeds what the single added model comparison establishes.
